COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
06.02.2024 ABA No. 82 of 2024
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Heard Mr. Abhishek Verma, learned
counsel through video conferencing along with
Mr. Dheeraj Joshi, learned counsel for the
applicants, as well as Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy
Advocate General along with Mr. S.C.Dumka,
learned AGA for the State and Mr. Piyush Garg,
learned counsel for the informant - Smt. Sheetal
Mund.
2. This Anticipatory Bail Application is
moved by the applicants in connection with FIR
No. 453 of 2023 under Sections 420, 465, 467,
468, 471, 120-B & 506 of IPC, registered at P.S.
Patel Nagar, Dehradun.
3. I have perused the First Information
Report.
4. From the bare perusal of the First
Information Report, it appears that the accused
persons, including the present applicants is a
gang which is being operated in District Dehradun
and Saharanpur, whereby forged power of
attorneys are being prepared and on the strength
of the power of attorney, the lands of the land
owners, like the informant, are being sold to
different persons.

4. In the case at hand, the informant has
lodged the First Information Report against those
persons including the applicants contending that
she is the owner of the land comprising in khsra
Nos. 372(ka), 372(kha0, 372(ga), 372(gha),
371(ga), 372(da),373, 374 and 375 of Majra,
Dehradun, District Dehradun, This land belonged
to her father and after the death of her father -
Sadhu Singh, the informant is the only legal heir
of late Sadhu Singh, who purchased this land 75
years ago and the said land was already recorded
in the revenue records in the name of the
informant-Sheetal Mandu.
5. According to the contents of the first
information report, a forged power of attorney of
the mother of the informant was prepared in
village Nakud of District Saharanpur by the
accused persons and it is averred in the first
information report that the mother of the
informant had never visited village Nakud and the
power of attorney was a forged one, which was
prepared by Bhajan Singh @ Harbhajan Singh S/of
Tej Singh, Prakash Singh S/o Bhagwan Singh and
Gurdeep Singh S/o Bhagwan Singh and
accordingly, the first information report was
lodged against these persons by the mother of

the informant and a charge-sheet under Sections
420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC was submitted by the
Investigating Agency against those persons.
6. Now, after taking the benefit of the
said power of attorney, the land transaction has
been entered into between them.
7. So far as the applicants are concerned,
the applicant accused No. 1 was gifted the land of
the informant through a gift deed by one
Sukhvinder Singh, who purchased this land, using
the forged power of attorney which was prepared
by the accused person and the applicant No. 2
filed an Original Suit No. 22 of 2017, Sukhvinder
Singh Vs. Smt. Niranjan Kaur and Sheetal in the
Court of Civil Judge, Dehradun, in which the
applicant No. 2 was the power of attorney holder
and Mr. Sukhvinder Singh is the person, who
purchased the land by way of a forged power of
attorney.
8. Having considered the allegations
levelled in the first information report which are
very serious, I do not find any reason to grant
anticipatory bail to the applicants, the same is
hereby rejected.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 Vacation Judge
 06.02.2024
Mahinder/
